lesson: Uploaded normal maps may use the other (DirectX) convention: measure each map against its own height map, flip green in a copy, and prove it with raking-light panels (normal-only versus real displacement must agree).
source: Coal mine story log 2-3; lib/prepare_textures.py comment; tests/test_swatches.py
plugin_evidence: Rule 'Normal maps are OpenGL, green up' (skills/surfaces-wear-and-construction/surface-recipes.md rule 2) and normals-test with a flipped control (blender-5-traps / the-required-steps 'shortcuts that fail'). But kit/place-kit/place_kit/checks/normals_test.py lines 9-10 say maps the kit did not make 'cannot be proved this way': the convention is read from the file NAME (nor_gl / nor_dx) or a declared property, not measured against the height map.
why: If the person uploads a texture pack with plain names, a small model following the plugin would pass a DirectX map as correct.

lesson: Smooth 8-bit height maps (wrap-around blur, percentile stretch) and save them as 16-bit so real displacement does not show 256-step stair banding.
plugin_evidence: No hit for 16-bit, banding or stair-stepping for heights anywhere in the plugin docs or kit (searched all md, py, js, json). The kit makes its own float heights (surfaces/heights.py) so it never meets the problem, but nothing warns a model that imports an 8-bit height map.
why: Only bites when someone feeds an 8-bit scan or uploaded height map into displacement.

lesson: Real relief must be small: a 30 cm relief looked like grass spikes; tuned to mud 6 cm, gravel 4 cm, brick 3 cm (slate 4, metal 1.6). Do not make tiles smaller than the defaults except on small objects.
source: Coal mine story log 3; Notes for the six builders; mine_common.SURFACES
plugin_evidence: surface-recipes.md: mud 'displacement 6 cm ... (judged, coal-mine yard)' (line ~53), slate 'depth 4 cm' (~81), brick 'depth 3 cm (judged, coal mine)' (~123), iron 1.6 cm; film-settings place_surfaces numbers. The 'spikes' symptom itself is not described.
why: Numbers are carried, so a model starts from sane depths.

lesson: A test panel at exactly the floor height rendered pure black: coplanar faces flicker or go black; keep surfaces 1-2 cm apart, and find the cause by varying one thing (lift 2 cm, normal strength 0).
source: Coal mine story log 3; tests/test_black_ground.py; Notes for the six builders 'Known facts'
plugin_evidence: LLM tips and tricks.md section 8 item 4 'Never put two surfaces on one plane (leave about 1 cm)'; construction-and-scale.md 'Coplanar faces' and 'Two faces that fight (z-fighting) are fixed by moving one of them 1 cm'; model_lint.py same-plane check.
why: Cheap to hit again in any scene with a flat panel on a floor.

lesson: When displacement is on, lower the normal-map strength to 0.6 times; the pair did not double the relief.
source: mine_common.surface_material (normal_strength x 0.6 when true_displacement); Notes for the six builders
plugin_evidence: surface-recipes.md 'multiply it by 0.6 (judged, coal-mine yard)'; SKILL.md 'Normal map and displacement together'; DEVIATIONS.md D7 gives the measured table (no doubling).
why: A real conflict with the Scenario skill's 'never both' that the plugin settled with a measurement.

lesson: Use real displacement on the big close-up surfaces that carry the picture (brick walls, slate roof, mud, gravel, ballast), not on small ones; watch render time.
source: Notes for the six builders; Coal mine story ('brick, slate, mud and gravel show real bumps')
plugin_evidence: kit/place-kit/data/roles.json marks only nine roles as displace (dirt road, mud, forest floor, stone paving, gravel, rock ground, earth, stone wall, thatch); wall.brick and roof.slate have displace=false, and surfaces.json gives brick and slate displacement_depth null, although surface-recipes.md line ~123 quotes brick 'depth 3 cm (judged, coal mine)'.
why: A brick engine house built by the plugin would get normal maps only, not the real bumps the mine photo showed.

lesson: Real displacement is heavy: peak memory 1.8 GB at 540x960 and 4.7 GB at 1080x1920 with dicing 2 pixels; raise the dicing number (3-4) if memory is short; adaptive subdivision with simple subdivision keeps faces flat.
plugin_evidence: kit/film-settings.json place_surfaces.displacement_dicing_rate_pixels [1,2] and place_audit.card_memory_gigabytes_max 12 (the audit can fail on memory), but no document says memory grows with output size or which knob to turn; the adaptive-subdivision recipe is not in the docs.
why: A displaced ground at final size can crash a card or a shared computer.

lesson: Grade the terrain mesh: fine squares (0.12 m) near the camera growing 9 percent a step up to 5 m, one ground mesh for the whole yard.
plugin_evidence: surface-recipes.md line ~12 'squares of 0.12 m near the camera, each step 1.09 times bigger, out to 5 m'; film-settings place_surfaces.displacement_graded_grid_*; DEVIATIONS.md 'graded grid'.
why: Keeps displacement affordable.

lesson: Hide texture repeats: look the picture up twice (second at 0.79 scale, offset), blend by slow noise; add big slow light/dark patches (variation 0.25) and a per-object tint.
source: modules/ground_and_yard.break_up_repeating_tiles; mine_common 'variation'; Notes for the six builders
plugin_evidence: surface-recipes.md rule 6 'Hide repeats: look the picture up twice, the second at 0.79 scale and offset 0.37 and 0.58 ... give every object its own small tint and offset'; film-settings place_surfaces.repeat_hiding.
why: Tiling is visible on every large ground or wall; the exact numbers are carried.

lesson: Make distant ground quiet: shrink small bumps to a quarter of strength and fade painted flecks with distance so far ground does not shimmer like water.
plugin_evidence: No hit for shimmer, farness or distance fade of normal strength; the wear layers and surface recipes have no distance input.
why: Distant ground shimmer is a common fault in stills and especially in moving shots.

lesson: One graded ground mesh with a material driven by stored attributes (wetness, farness, coal dust in a colour attribute); two overlapping ground meshes show a seam or fight.
plugin_evidence: surface-recipes.md rule 9 'keep to one ground mesh with a material driven by attributes where you can ... The coal-mine yard did it with one graded ground mesh'; the plugin itself uses plan masks instead of vertex colours.
why: Prevents z-fighting between road, verge and ground.

lesson: Puddles: lay each water sheet just above the lowest ground it covers, dig the bed about 4 cm under it, flatten the broad slope across the puddle so it is not deep on the uphill side, let the sheet run 20 cm under the raised rim, add a faint ripple so the mirror is not CG-clean (IOR 1.33).
plugin_evidence: surface-recipes.md line ~54 'puddle hollows 4 cm deep (judged, same yard); shine in the hollows (roughness 0.3, measured)'; wear-recipes puddle depth shares; roads verb makes puddle hollows. Levelling the slope, the hidden edge and the ripple are not written down.
why: Fine detail; the kit's roads step does part of it in code.

lesson: Build thousands of small shapes into ONE mesh per material group (one builder per material), under about 300k triangles per part before displacement.
source: Notes for the six builders 'Efficiency'; MeshBuilder in mine_common.py
plugin_evidence: skills/make-3d-models/blender-mcp-notes.md B15 'join parts that share a material (232 parts to 19)' (card-model route); DEVIATIONS.md 'plants and litter ... built in numpy and joined per kind'; film-settings place_audit.triangles_per_builder_max 1,500,000. No guidance for a builder writing its own bulk-shape code.
why: Object count, not triangles, is what slows Blender scripts and exports.

lesson: Work out picture coordinates automatically from world position and tile size so bricks run level, slate courses run across the slope, and wood grain runs along the length.
plugin_evidence: surface-recipes.md rule 5 'UV first ... box UV per face in metres for walls ... planks: u along the length, v across'; `explainer-film-place surfaces/finish` writes the UVs itself.
why: Stretched or mirrored textures were a named failure in the mine brief.

lesson: Make sure faces point outward and check inside-out per closed piece: the delivery check found 73 inside-out headframe parts (69 bars, both winding wheels, 2 trims) that nobody saw; as shipped it also gave a useless 908 errors because of a 3.5 km sky dome.
source: Textures story log 23; mine_common MeshBuilder winding note; garden/addon/tests/audit_courtyard_with_addon_lessons.py (winding per closed component)
plugin_evidence: construction-and-scale.md line ~87 'Inside-out closed parts fail'; place_audit inside_out_parts_allowed 0. But kit/place-kit/place_kit/checks/construction.py lines 167-172 and 394 add up the signed volume of the WHOLE object, so one inverted bar inside a joined mesh (positive total volume) is not caught; the sky-dome noise is not mentioned.
why: Joined headframe-style meshes are exactly where the inside-out parts hid.

lesson: A building needs a floor: the ground part dug 7 cm out under the engine house, nobody built a floor, and the doorway looked onto the void; assign cross-part things like this in the briefs.
plugin_evidence: construction-and-scale.md 'a floor, and a threshold, so a doorway looks onto something (the coal-mine engine house once had a door onto nothing)'; check 'Doorway floor' (within 0.30 m below the sill); ownership contracts in place-planner.md.
why: A classic gap between parts built in parallel.

lesson: Smoke from a chimney first looked like giant black balloons: make the plume thin, light, irregular, leaving on a rising path, growing wider with distance, dark near the chimney and lighter far away, and keep it clear of other structures.
source: Coal mine story log 6-7; modules/chimney_and_smoke.py header
plugin_evidence: The plugin sends smoke to the live effects layer (build-and-paint-a-place SKILL 'plan_effects.py wind'; paint-prompt.txt forbids smoke in the painting). Nothing says how to model a smoke plume as 3D meshes for a Blender picture.
why: Only matters for stills drawn straight from Blender with chimneys.

lesson: First assembly check: the biggest foreground structure hid the main building, the foreground was a field of rubble, and the track was bent toward the camera to sweep across the bottom like the reference; compare with the reference picture and move things.
plugin_evidence: LLM tips and tricks.md section 4 items 9-11 (nothing big and dark bottom-left, fill the bottom third with the story, props touch or stand apart) and item 16 (match the liked picture by landmarks). No rule about a foreground landmark hiding the main building or about a curved lead-in line.
why: Composition rules exist but are written for a street between buildings.

lesson: Light a dusk scene with a soft warm fill from the camera's side so mud and brick show their own warm colours (not only cool sky light), tuned by comparing about ten small test photos with the reference screenshot.
source: Coal mine story log 7; assemble_mine.add_front_fill_light; courtyard 'cool fill from camera side'
plugin_evidence: the-required-steps.md Step 7 (sun, sky, 'a softer fill from the opposite side so shadows are not black'; value study under 0.5 percent clipped) and the new variations tool (batched-rounds-and-card-time.md, about 10 far-apart versions on one sheet). The fill-from-the-camera-side colour trick and reference-matched exposure are not written.
why: Decides whether the place looks like the reference mood or just lit.

lesson: A batch of test cameras silently used the same camera three times (settings typed the wrong way): look at the pictures, not only the script.
plugin_evidence: tips section 0 item 5 'Never trust a single still' and place-builder.md 'look at it with the Read tool'; the new variations tool (batched-rounds-and-card-time.md lines ~65-67) flags pairs of VERSIONS whose pictures came out nearly the same through every camera. Two identical cameras in one job (the mine's case) are not checked by it or by a plain `render` job.
why: Cheap to add; the batch tool covers a neighbouring fault, not this one.

lesson: Photo settings that worked: Cycles, OpenImageDenoise, adaptive threshold 0.015, bounces 6/3/4, indirect sample clamp 8, AgX Punchy, exposure 0.4-0.5; 128 samples took 8 min 11 s at 1080x1920 on 4 processors.
source: assemble_mine.py; Coal mine story log 9; courtyard build_courtyard.py (180 samples 13 min)
plugin_evidence: rendering-on-rented-cards.md section 8 'Cycles: OptiX denoise, adaptive threshold 0.01, light tree on ... finals 2400 x 1600 at 512' and the 40 s card time (line ~27). The indirect clamp (fireflies) and view-transform look are not mentioned; AgX appears only in pit-village scripts.
why: Fireflies from small bright lamps are a predictable problem.

lesson: Be honest about flaws: list known rough edges in each module and report, say what was never rendered, and when helpers are stopped on request say their findings do not exist.
source: Coal mine story 'Where things stand'; Notes for the six builders (known_flaws in report); courtyard 'Not checked'
plugin_evidence: agents/place-builder.md return fields 'unsure, failures, not_tested' and 'Never write that something passed when you did not see it pass' (lines ~109-125); skills/make-explainer-film/house-rules.md 'Say what you tested, what you did not'.
why: The person relies on the 'not tested' lines.

lesson: Parallel builders: read the shared toolbox but never edit it, touch only your own files, build in world coordinates on the shared ground height, never make cameras/world/lights unless told, never touch git, return a report with counts and flaws.
plugin_evidence: agents/place-builder.md sections 2-3 (yours / not yours / frozen, own stage file, 'Do not commit or push', report fields); kit/place-kit/data/templates/part_brief.md; house-rules.md 'never let parallel helpers edit shared files'.
why: The plugin's owner/stage-file design is a stricter version of the same rules.

lesson: Cap the CPU threads of each Blender run (-t 2) so six helpers on one computer do not starve each other.
source: Notes for the six builders 'Run Blender like this'
plugin_evidence: No hit for '-t 2', threads or starving in agents, skills, workflow or kit docs; tips section 8 item 8 says only 'One heavy job at a time'. workflows/build-a-place.js has a maxParallelBuilders cap (default 4, 'use 2 on a slow computer') but passes no thread limit to Blender.
why: Parallel builders on one shared machine is exactly how the plugin's workflow runs.

lesson: Preview each part alone (stand-in ground or neutral light, three angles: front-left three-quarter like the reference, a close detail, a back or side view), look at the pictures next to the design picture, and fix before moving on.
source: Notes for the six builders; previews/*.py
plugin_evidence: agents/place-builder.md step 6 'Look at your work ... with the Read tool'; place-planner.md item 10 'at least three views'; part_brief.md section B 'FOLLOW ... DO NOT COPY'.
why: Keeps each builder honest before the combine.

lesson: Keep preview pictures small (900 px or less, 40 samples or less, about 2 minutes each) on a shared computer.
plugin_evidence: agents/place-builder.md 'Run only small tests on this computer ... small pictures, --quick'; film-settings place_render local previews (480 x 320 at 8 samples EEVEE, 320 x 240 at 16 Cycles).
why: Matches the plugin's slow-computer rule.

lesson: Lit windows: panes shine one way and do not light the room, so the inside is black; vary the brightness pane to pane and put dark shapes (a pillar, blind, curtain) just inside the glass so the glow does not read as a flat lamp; tune glow strength in the final light.
source: modules/engine_house.py KNOWN_FLAWS and window code; village_and_sky KNOWN_FLAWS ('no interiors and no curtains')
plugin_evidence: the-required-steps.md Step 7 'a real lamp inside every lit window or lantern (a light inside its own glow box is blocked in Cycles)'; tips section 7 item 5 'Glowing things get a black base colour'; blender-mcp-notes C1 'shallow interior box' behind an opening (card-model route). The varied-brightness and shapes-behind-glass trick is not carried.
why: Makes dusk windows read as lived in.

lesson: A painted dusk sky used as the world picture is only 8-bit (no true bright sun): brighten the glow inside the world nodes and keep the sun as a separate lamp; add tiny noise so smooth shades do not band; it goes soft when enlarged into a tall frame.
plugin_evidence: kit/place-kit/place_kit/light.py adds a sun and a plain sky colour when the scene has none; build-and-paint-a-place SKILL section 7 uses `skyCard` for the painted sky in the film page. Nothing about 8-bit world pictures, banding or sun plus sky consistency.
why: Only for scenes that use a painted world picture.

lesson: Wrap the world in an all-round backdrop: three rings of hills all the way round, lighter and bluer when far (haze by colour), real geometry for parallax, camera clip end 1000 m or more, plain ground continued to the horizon so no other camera ever sees empty sky and a dark slab.
source: modules/village_and_sky.py; Garden plan 30 section 3 item 1 and builder 4; Courtyard log 5 and 9
plugin_evidence: No rule for a backdrop in any skill, agent or doc (grep for hills, backdrop, horizon finds only the film page's `kit.backdrop` for paper cards); clip_end 1500 is set only inside pit-village scripts (assemble_lockout.py, assemble_notice_corner.py). place-planner.md asks for at least three views but nothing makes the world work from all of them.
why: The plugin demands several views per place; the garden's veranda view showed the missing backdrop at once.

lesson: The ground is a rectangle with hard edges and a tall bank at the rim (12 m high about 100 m out) can cover the low hills: another part must hide the rim, and the bank should fade out beyond about 60 m.
source: modules/ground_and_yard.py and village_and_sky.py KNOWN_FLAWS; ground_height() in mine_common
plugin_evidence: No hit for ground rim, terrain edge or bank covering hills. The plugin's graded ground (surfaces/ground_mesh.py) makes a rectangular grid with no edge treatment.
why: Edge of the ground showing is a basic outdoor fault.

lesson: Exaggerate thin, small readable parts for distance (rails 1.45 times real, large carts) and say so; chunky readable shapes beat tiny detail.
source: modules/track_and_carts.py KNOWN_FLAWS; Notes for the six builders
plugin_evidence: style-rule-and-measures.md 'few, bigger, cleaner marks'; paint 'Find every wire, rung and bar under 6 px wide: remove, thicken, or name it' (tips section 9 item 4). The scale check (place_scale: warn beyond the range, fail beyond 1.5 times) has no 'deliberate exaggeration, noted' path.
why: A model may fail its own scale check for a good stylistic reason.

lesson: Angular lumps (coal, stones) made as flat-faced convex shapes look CG-sharp and glint close up; later on the street coal chips read as faceted gems and straw as matchsticks, so make flat irregular lumps and short, thin, curved straw.
plugin_evidence: surface-recipes.md line ~85 'straw: loose strands as 3D litter pieces (thin, curved, short: the street's first straws looked like matchsticks)'; species.json litter shapes. 'Faceted gems' for lumps is not recorded.
why: Small, but visible in close views.

lesson: The person told the helpers NOT to use the film plugin (and a word was ambiguous, so the Astra add-on was left out too and this was written in the story).
source: Coal mine story 'The goal'; Notes for the six builders 'Plain Blender only'
plugin_evidence: The REQUIRED header (SKILL.md line ~9 of surfaces-wear-and-construction, make-3d-models and build-and-paint-a-place) says 'Do it without being asked', README says the pass runs 'even when the request names no surfaces', and hooks/place-reminder.py prints the reminder at every matching prompt; only skills/make-explainer-film/house-rules.md line 4 says 'Follow them unless the user's own instructions say otherwise' (house rules only). Nothing says an explicit 'do not use the plugin' wins over the hook and the REQUIRED header.
why: The person tests ideas with and without the plugin; the plugin's loud 'REQUIRED' wording could override that.

lesson: The add-on built for Blender 5.1 broke on 5.2 because geometry-nodes modifier inputs moved from mod[identifier] to mod.properties.inputs.<identifier>.value: patch with a small shim in your own script and leave the person's add-on untouched.
plugin_evidence: blender-5-traps.md lists 16 traps and none is this one; grep for properties.inputs or geometry-nodes modifier input finds nothing. The general habit 'work around a fault in a shared file, do not edit it' is in place-builder.md line ~39.
why: Any script that sets geometry-nodes inputs on 5.2 will hit it; it cost the first courtyard test.

lesson: Blender 5.2 renamed a sky setting; use the new name (check the API instead of memory).
plugin_evidence: blender-mcp-notes.md D17 'Do not trust memory for API names. Look them up with get_python_api_docs' and blender-5-traps.md as a list; this particular rename is not listed.
why: The general rule is carried; the specific rename is not.

lesson: Tool limits are part of the brief: the add-on refuses stones thinner than 0.2 m or more than six times longer than thick, so shapes were made thicker.
plugin_evidence: The add-on is deliberately not in the plugin (kit/place-kit/SOURCES-AND-LICENCES.md lines 31-32: only the 'rules they teach' were kept) and this stone rule is not among them.
why: Add-on specific.

lesson: A backdrop made of ordinary lit geometry washed the first picture out (a huge green sheet floated at the top): use flat, unlit hazy ridgelines and switch their shadow visibility off so they never block the sun.
source: Courtyard story log 5 and 9; build_courtyard.py ridge() comment 'a painted backdrop: it must not block the sun'
plugin_evidence: No document or rule about backdrop shadow visibility. The idea is used once, for people only: kit/calculators/plan_lights.py line ~846 'Figures: visible_shadow off, each with a soft foot patch'. Nothing for hills, sky domes or ground planes; the Garden plan said 'use object ray visibility if you need to separate things'.
why: Without it the sun can silently do nothing (see the next lesson).

lesson: Make the key feature readable from the real camera: the pond hid behind the bridge and rocks and read as dark ground, so the pond was enlarged, the hall moved back, the camera raised and lily pads added.
plugin_evidence: place-planner.md item 11 'List 12 to 16 readable features' with the blind reader at half size (place-checker.md Mode blind_reader; reading test 12 of 16 in style-rule-and-measures.md).
why: The blind reading test is the plugin's version of this check.

lesson: A scripted build that makes thousands of leaves one object at a time gets slower as it goes (7 minutes); building them in bulk with arrays took about 10 seconds.
plugin_evidence: No hit for foreach_set bulk building, quadratic slowdown or per-object slowness. The plugin's own growth code builds pieces in numpy and joins them (DEVIATIONS.md) but no doc tells a model writing its own scatter code.
why: Slow builds waste card and computer time on every leafy place.

lesson: Trees: maple leaves as chunky balls looked like popcorn; use flat pointed leaves over a dark core, later leaves at real size (5-12 cm, not 20-34 cm), about seven lobes, a crown in separate layers with windows so trunk and low sun show, translucent leaves, colours from deep red to a few yellow-green and brown.
source: Courtyard story log 8; Garden plan 30 builder 2 and Textures log 30-31
plugin_evidence: worked-examples-garden-and-canal-lock.md line ~109 'Maple leaves went from 20 to 34 cm wide to 5 to 12 cm (the real size) and were counted at 56,000'; surface-recipes.md 'foliage cards ... chunky clumps'. The crown layering, translucency and colour range are not written as rules, and species.json has no trees.
why: Trees are the most noticed saturated element in many places.

lesson: A low sun did nothing: a 4 m hall with the sun low behind it throws a shadow about 25 m long over the whole garden, and hazy hills were also blocking the sun; place the sun and remove blocking walls (shadow length is height divided by tan of the sun's elevation).
source: Courtyard story log 9; Garden plan 30 (9 degree sun: 1 cm rake ridge throws a 6 cm shadow)
plugin_evidence: No hit for shadow length, low sun geometry or a wall blocking the sun. The only sun guidance is light.py (a 35 degree sun when the scene has none) and tips section 7 about few shadow-casting lights.
why: The 'sun does nothing' fault looks like a bad material and costs several rounds.

lesson: A thin golden haze (volume) gave soft beams but dimmed the picture and killed the sky's glow, so it was dropped; depth should come from colour and selective edge loss, not a veil that erases the main building.
source: Courtyard story log 10; Garden plan 30 section 4 'Atmosphere'
plugin_evidence: No hit for haze, volume or mist in the plugin's Blender guidance (only the film page's DustBurst and Motes).
why: A known time-waster; one line would save a test.

lesson: A mysterious white shape was found by hiding object groups one at a time: it was the pond mirroring the glowing paper screens; roughen the water slightly, dim the screens, and later hide the hall lamps from reflections.
source: Courtyard story log 11; Textures log 30; build_courtyard.py --hide option
plugin_evidence: No hit for bisecting by hiding groups or for reflections of emissive surfaces in water; the plugin only says 'Read the render log' and 'Look at 100 percent crops'.
why: A debugging method that works for any unexplained mark in a picture.

lesson: Final render time on this computer (2400x1600, 180 samples) was 13 minutes; a rented card does it in under a minute.
plugin_evidence: rendering-on-rented-cards.md section 2 'A rented card draws a 2400 x 1600 final in about 40 s (measured ...)'; place_card_time estimates.
why: Numbers are carried and measured.

lesson: Prove two versions of a tool give an identical scene: fingerprint everything built (including evaluated geometry), compare, and also compare the pictures dot for dot (0 of 345,600 dots differed).
plugin_evidence: `explainer-film-place fingerprint` and `ownership-diff` (SKILL.md verb table); README 'drawing twice gives the same picture' tests; the new variations tool puts values back and checks a fingerprint. The pixel-diff of two tool versions is not a documented recipe.
why: Good basis for 'does my change alter anything else'.

lesson: Test a tool's cleanup by forcing a late failure and counting the data blocks (objects, meshes, materials, node groups) left behind; a safety net should clean up but still show the error.
plugin_evidence: `explainer-film-place undo` exists, and test_place_fixes.py tests undo, but no document tells a model to test cleanup this way (no hit for left behind / rollback in skills or agents).
why: Useful when building or accepting any scripted tool.

lesson: Open an uploaded add-on safely: unpack into its own folder, read its guide first, search its code for anything risky (internet, starting programs, deleting files), open it with autoexec off, run it only on copies.
source: Courtyard story log 1; Textures log 23 (read every file twice before installing skills)
plugin_evidence: agents/place-builder.md and build-and-paint-a-place SKILL use `blender -b --disable-autoexec`; nothing tells a model to read or search third-party code first.
why: The person uploads other people's code and skills.

lesson: Do not edit the person's add-on; load it from its folder and keep fixes in your own loader or shim, then say so.
source: Courtyard story log 2 and README; astra_loader.py
plugin_evidence: place-builder.md line ~39 'If you find a fault in a shared file, work around it and write it in shared_problems. Do not edit the shared file'; ownership rules (never edit another owner's material).
why: Same discipline, written for builders.

lesson: Fresh timber from a tool comes out orange: pull it to silvery grey-brown; very pale pebbles blow out in raking sun: tone them down.
source: Courtyard story (build_courtyard.py comments); Garden plan 30 surfaces
plugin_evidence: surface-recipes.md 'timber_weathered ... silvered grey-brown #9b8476 ... not salmon' (judged, garden); value study in the-required-steps.md Step 7. Pebble/low-sun blow-out is not recorded.
why: Palette detail for the garden.

lesson: Patterned ground such as raked gravel needs mesh finer than the pattern (at least four mesh squares per line: a 2.5 cm mesh for 12 cm lines), lines about 12 cm apart and 1.5 cm high, rings round rocks; a golden-hour sun 9 degrees up makes a 1 cm ridge throw a 6 cm shadow, and 2.5-3 cm looks ploughed.
source: Garden plan 30 builder 1 item 4 and section 4 'Rake depth'; Courtyard log (rake lines by shading only)
plugin_evidence: worked-examples-garden-and-canal-lock.md line ~110 mentions 'straight rake lines every 12 cm, about 1.5 cm high' only as a result; no rule for mesh resolution against pattern period.
why: The resolution-versus-period rule applies to any line pattern (planks, tile joints).

lesson: Hold rocks and stones low and grouped: buried about a third (22 percent before), grouped in threes with different heights, never in a row, none wider at the top than at the base, moss collars at the feet.
source: Garden plan 30 builder 1 item 3; real-garden research
plugin_evidence: surface-recipes.md 'stone_rubble ... half-buried' and worked-examples line ~111 'Rocks were to be set about a third into the ground (22 percent before; judged)'. Grouping and base rules are not carried.
why: Garden specific, but 'half-buried stone' is a general realism cue.

lesson: The person's renderer rule: Cycles for plates and frames where lamps, windows or fires are lit; EEVEE when they are off ('worth it, but only for scenes where the lights are on').
plugin_evidence: rendering-on-rented-cards.md section 1; surfaces SKILL 'Cycles when lit'; place-kit renderer_choice.py (`renderer-for`); hooks and agents repeat it.
why: A standing decision, carried in several places.

lesson: Later goal: use the full 3D set for an immersive moving camera through the street, with lighting reacting to characters moving around; Cycles then gives characters real shadows and reflections for free.
source: Textures story Goal ('Later goal, 21 October') and log 26
plugin_evidence: No hit for immersive, characters moving, or lighting that reacts to people anywhere in the plugin; the film route is still 'paint over one plate and project it'.
why: Tells a builder to model the whole place (all sides, interiors, people) rather than one facade.

lesson: Calibrate every measuring tool with controls before trusting it: a shuffled copy must score about 0.99, a blurred copy 0.17, another surface 0.09; a first version scored 0 on height even for alike pictures, so it was loosened and retested.
plugin_evidence: Tests with controls exist (normals-test flipped copy, picture_measures blurred copy and the opposite-pictures fault in DEVIATIONS.md item 11), and fresh-checkers.md says a checker 'can over-trust the builders' own test files'. No general rule 'give every new metric a positive and a negative control'.
why: A metric that cannot fail is the commonest false comfort.

lesson: Blender's noise, cell and wave nodes do not tile even at whole-number scales (a shop page claimed they do): test claims before use; make tiles from periodic functions.
plugin_evidence: blender-5-traps.md item 10 'Blender's noise, cell and wave nodes do not tile'; heights.py periodic_noise.
why: Carried with its fix.

lesson: Make normal maps from heights at a calibrated steepness (the steepest 1 percent of slopes tilt the normal 26-34 degrees) with whole-number-like strengths; too low does nothing, too high looks like plastic.
plugin_evidence: surface-recipes.md 'map steepness ... 26 to 34 degrees (judged, from the garden)'; film-settings place_surfaces.steepest_one_percent_tilt_degrees.
why: Carried.

lesson: Colour-setting traps: data pictures wrongly set to colour inside a wetness layer (found by an audit); a single-channel picture saved into the red channel only (found by a researcher).
plugin_evidence: surface-recipes.md rule 1 (colour sRGB, data Non-Color), blender-5-traps.md items 1-2, normals-test and place audit 'Non-Color'. The single-channel save fault is not mentioned.
why: Mostly carried.

lesson: Outside tools were checked and judged: Ucupaint and Material Maker run with workarounds but are no closer than Blender nodes (borrow ideas only); a small 'MCP Blender Agent' cannot set node settings and has no password (skip).
plugin_evidence: No hit for Ucupaint, Material Maker or MCP Blender Agent anywhere in the plugin.
why: Saves a model from re-evaluating the same tools.

lesson: When the disk is nearly full delete only things that can be made again (downloaded programs, duplicate copies of big pictures); keep big files on the rented store.
plugin_evidence: blender-5-traps.md item 16 'Free disk ... if free space falls under about 0.4 GB, stop and report'; film-settings place_render.disk_free_gigabytes_stop_here 0.4. 'Delete only re-makeable things' is not written.
why: Disk filled several times in the project.

lesson: A fresh checker followed every link in the cookbook (320, none broken) and re-read 55 numbers against the files (9 wrong, fixed); one word for one thing.
plugin_evidence: `explainer-film-setup` checks that every kit file the skills name exists (LLM tips section 20 item 3); `explainer-film-place check-presets` checks every number has a kind and a source; fresh-checkers.md re-reads claims. No instruction to re-read a document's numbers against its files before release.
why: Wrong numbers in guides were found by checkers three times.

lesson: After a machine restart a second helper checked every item on disk, redid only what was missing or cut short, and nothing done before the restart was lost.
source: Textures story log 11; Garden character log 31 (container restarted twice)
plugin_evidence: fresh-checkers.md line ~70 'A container restart can lose a checker's work ... save results to files as you go'; place-builder.md 'Save your evidence ... as you go'. The recovery procedure (audit what is on disk, redo only the missing) is not written.
why: Restarts happened repeatedly.

lesson: Build wear as separate layers in one recipe (layout, colour and fade, damage, moss, outline and shadow), each with its own seed, mask and amount; switching a layer off or changing its seed changes nothing outside it (proved 0.0 percent) except one declared link (moss avoids fresh damage).
plugin_evidence: place_kit/wear/layer_base.py header: AMOUNT 0 gives EXACTLY the input, own Seed, fixed interface; README 'Amount 0 gives exactly the picture without the layer'. The 'declared link' between layers is not carried.
why: The layered design is the plugin's core; a small piece is missing.

lesson: Express recipe sizes as shares of the tile so one picture comes out the same at 512, 1254 and 2508 pixels (resolution independence).
plugin_evidence: The plugin sizes marks in picture dots instead (wear-recipes.md 'Marks are sized in picture dots') and has no resolution-independence rule for tiles.
why: Matters when maps are redrawn at a new size.

lesson: Tune on several random seeds: the seed that was tuned scores 0.04-0.08 higher than others; quote scores beside plain ones when a measured-once curve lifts them; most of a gain came from one jumpy measure.
plugin_evidence: No hit for tuning on several seeds or for reporting a gain with and without a jumpy measure; the plugin labels numbers measured/judged/invented, which is related but not the same.
why: Stops overfitting a look to one seed.

lesson: Judge procedural marks for flaws a checker found: paint tongues instead of broad flat bands, flat khaki moss with sharp teeth, chips gathering in L-shapes, ruler-straight rows and square corners, drippy shadows, round lichen dots, 'fresh and clean' losing the painted look.
plugin_evidence: wear-recipes.md 'Things that already went wrong' (weeds in puddles, moss cut-outs, over-even cracks, sticker moss, bean-bag cushions) and 'no two siblings alike' (the-required-steps.md); the slate-specific list is not carried.
why: Many are slate-specific; the principle (irregular, not ruled) is carried.

lesson: Stop after the allowed rounds and report what is left (about 14 slates with cut-glass facets were not fixed because the job allowed two rounds).
source: Textures story log 15; Garden character log 31
plugin_evidence: film-settings place_checks.fix_rounds 1; fresh-checkers.md line ~34 'One fix round, then stop'; build-a-place.js 'exactly one fix round'.
why: Bounded rounds with honest leftovers.

lesson: When the person supplies their own maps, give each board its own random strip of BOTH colour and height maps from the same place (so colour and relief match), with flips, small zoom and tone changes, landmarks shown only now and then, and one switch between an exactly repeating tile and a big area of new boards.
plugin_evidence: surface-recipes.md rule 5: 'random offset for each plank, and mirror or turn some planks and switch the knot off on about half'. The use of the person's own maps (both maps from one place) is not covered because the plugin makes its own heights.
why: Tied to the person's uploaded wood.

lesson: Measure repetition with a twin test: share of pieces that have a twin (0-2 percent good, 14-18 percent poor, 100 percent for a plain repeat).
plugin_evidence: No hit for twin or repetition share; the audit only lists siblings that are exact copies (place_wear.shape_sibling_copy_share_max).
why: A quick number for 'does it repeat'.

lesson: Long boards: a layout whose boards are about 2.5 times longer than high, with straight full-height joints and even rows reads as stacked stone, not planks; a source one tile long cannot give longer boards.
plugin_evidence: surface-recipes.md gives plank widths (9-17 cm) and gaps but no length or joint-stagger rule.
why: Plank floors and decks are common in places.

lesson: Builders' claims must be recomputed: 'never the same strip as its neighbour' was really 19 percent; 9.8 percent moss was really 0.6 percent; a report said nothing vanished though 58 materials were dropped.
source: Textures story log 16; Garden character log 31
plugin_evidence: fresh-checkers.md lines 7-12 (all three examples), place-builder.md 'Write each CLAIM as a bare sentence ... A fresh checker will recompute', film-settings place_checks.claims_recheck.
why: One of the most valuable lessons, fully carried.

lesson: Masks made by an image model as stamp sheets were not better than node-made shapes (US$0.354 for six sheets; black backgrounds 4 of 6 times, round fluffy balls, rubber-stamp look; scores within noise): do not spend on them unless the shapes are generated from a crop of the person's own picture.
plugin_evidence: No hit for stamp sheets or generated masks as layers in the plugin.
why: A cheap-to-skip paid experiment.

lesson: Wetness layer rules: water in low spots (road camber to gutter) as puddles that flatten stones and mirror lamps; wet stone darker and glossier with drier tops; walls darker wet foot and streaks under sills; one wetness node group that sits between the dry look and the shader.
plugin_evidence: wear-recipes.md layer table (wetness: 'low places and rut bottoms; ground within 1.5 m of any water'), layer order, 'Wetness colours' lines ~73-76; place_kit/wear/layers/wetness.py; film-settings place_wear.puddle_depth_shares.
why: Carried as code and as numbers.

lesson: The roughness map makes the road look wet (0.28); the specularity map changed it by only 0.006; and none of the .glb maps reach the film because the projected painting covers 98 percent of a moved view.
plugin_evidence: wear-recipes.md line ~73-76 'The roughness map does the work (dry about 0.9, wet about 0.3: measured); the specular map changed the road by only 0.006'; rendering-on-rented-cards.md. The 'does not reach the film' finding is not stated.
why: Explains why wet looks must be painted from the wet plate.

lesson: White grit on wet ground in EEVEE was soft-shadow noise, not the material: shadow rays 4, steps 16.
plugin_evidence: rendering-on-rented-cards.md section 8 'White speckle on wet ground was EEVEE's soft shadows, not the material'; place_render.eevee_shadow_rays/steps.
why: Carried with the numbers.

lesson: Wet walls first came out lighter than dry (wrong): wet walls 0.84 of dry, wet foot 0.66; the road was too bright (1.5 times); wet reading of walls at plate size stayed weak.
plugin_evidence: wear-recipes.md 'Wetness colours ... wet walls came out 0.84 of dry and the wet foot 0.66, and the first try made walls lighter when wet (wrong)'.
why: Carried.

lesson: On wet ground props must look seated: props stood dry and sacks looked as if they hovered, and the brazier-lit foreground read as polished tile with a blown-out glare pool.
plugin_evidence: Contact shadows under near props in the film page (build-and-paint-a-place section 7, plan_effects.py contact-shadows) and place_light.clip_share_max 0.005; nothing says props need the wetness layer and a dark seat, or how to tame a glare pool.
why: Visible in wet night scenes.

lesson: The painter brief must keep wet looks: remove 'matte painted finish' and the ban on puddles and reflections, ask to keep sheen, mirrored lamps and windows, gutter puddles, wet joints and darker wall feet where the wet plate has them.
plugin_evidence: surfaces SKILL 'Painter template words on wet places'; build-and-paint-a-place section 6 'Wet or dusk places'; kit/calculators/templates/paint-prompt.txt keep_wet and never_rest_wet; paint_request.py --keep-wetness.
why: Carried in four places.

lesson: The painter added heavy pale clouds despite three sentences against them: a plain dark sky was put in for free using Blender's exact sky outline (four tries to keep the thin rails clean).
plugin_evidence: kit/calculators/templates/paint-prompt.txt lines ~33-34 ban 'a moon, stars or bright clouds', but the ban did not hold in the project's tests; no step replaces the painted sky with a plate sky from a mask.
why: Costs a repaint on every sky-bearing plate.

lesson: Make the 'behind' painting from a props-free twin plate drawn in Blender that hides exactly the props the film's page hides (found by reading the page), repaint that, and match its brightness to the front painting for free; the old dry behind painting showed on 56-71 percent of the near road when the camera moved.
plugin_evidence: build-and-paint-a-place SKILL section 6 item 5 (behind painting made by asking the painter to paint the near props out of the lined-up painting) and make_behind_picture.py; no props-free twin plate route and no brightness-match step.
why: Keeps wet ground wet behind props and was the cheaper, truer route.

lesson: The film stage's finishing curve crushed the wet road to 0.7 of its painted brightness: a 'toe' switch plus easing the dark frame edge 0.30 to 0.25 brought it to 0.935 and left eight other scenes pixel-identical when off.
plugin_evidence: wear-recipes.md line ~61 'The darkest part of a mark stays at 0.10 or above (measured: the film's finishing curve crushes values under about 0.12)'. The stage code in kit/paper-film/stage/cinema-stage.js (vignette 0.32, lift 0.015) has no toe switch; kit-sync-notes.md does not list it.
why: Dark wet roads are crushed in the stage unless the fix is ported.

lesson: Joints between stones, bricks and planks vanish easily (6 of 22 lightings pass): make the joint darker, dull when wet and sloped at the stone edge, fade the slope with distance, do not cut real 8 mm grooves, and count every dot (18 of 22).
plugin_evidence: wear-recipes.md 'Joints (between stones, bricks and planks)' lines ~45-53 and style-rule-and-measures.md 'Readability under three lights' give the advice and the 6/22, 21/22, 18/22 numbers; surfaces.json cobble note. There is no joints layer or lighting test in the kit code.
why: Advice is carried; nothing enforces it.

lesson: Rubbish mask from the real shape of the street: gutters, wall feet, doorsteps, pipe and lamp-post feet, inside corners, rings round props, in patches, never on the middle of the road, gathering about 8 to 1 at the kerb.
plugin_evidence: place_kit/wear/layers/rubbish.py (wall feet, gutters, road edges, never on the crown or wheel track) and wear/masks.py masks Wall Dist, Prop Dist, Litter Dist, Dampness; wear-recipes.md layer table 'rubbish'.
why: The 8 to 1 ratio is not carried, the rest is.

lesson: Rendering traps from the joints work: a stale picture left on the rented machine came back as a black road, a plan picture was turned the wrong way round, four wrong explanations of one failure, about 60 runs against a plan of 40.
plugin_evidence: rendering-on-rented-cards.md line ~85 'Clear the remote output folder before a run (a stale picture once came back as a black road)'; blender-5-traps.md item 2 (image rows bottom-up, wrong-way pictures).
why: Two of the four traps are carried.

lesson: Scenario skills trial: their wear shows only in Cycles unless baked; their automatic UV seams failed on a door; the plugin's own layers stay better for walls and ground.
plugin_evidence: blender-mcp-notes.md line ~334 'For wear that must show in EEVEE, use the place kit's masks ... those show only in Cycles. Otherwise bake it'; SKILL.md conflict list.
why: Carried as a decision.

lesson: Light-and-dark study with blown and crushed shares is useful; a colour-setting audit is useful; their subject verdicts are built for faces.
plugin_evidence: the-required-steps.md Step 7 'a value study ... under 0.5 percent of dots clipped'; place_light.clip_share_max (source: the Scenario lighting skill); normals-test covers colour space.
why: Carried.

lesson: The 'web' export squeezes shapes lossily (up to 52 mm) and needs one line added to the stage; the export check found three real faults the exporter hides.
plugin_evidence: No hit for lossy export, 52 mm or quantisation in the plugin; blender-mcp-notes.md B13 lists exporter options without this warning.
why: Matters for the .glb card route only.

lesson: Written 'local rules' for skills are instructions, not locks: use gates that refuse (preflight stages) and a prompt-time reminder.
source: Textures story log 23 ('Unsure: whether Claude will always follow the written local rules')
plugin_evidence: hooks/place-reminder.py and hooks.json; preflight stage `place` and `plates --gate`; README 'NOT tested ... that a smaller model ... loads the skill by itself'.
why: The plugin was built around exactly this worry.

lesson: Before installing any skill, have helpers read every file twice, remove self-install lines, ask the person first (a skill runs with full permissions); repository copies filled the disk.
plugin_evidence: No hit for installing skills or reviewing third-party skills in the plugin.
why: Process rule for the person's own workspace.

lesson: Reusable weathering kit: every fact about one place lives in one settings file, looks are presets, everything goes on in one call and comes off leaving the scene exactly as it was; the courtyard took it from a settings file alone.
plugin_evidence: place-kit/README.md (settings file, looks, `undo`, 'Run twice it gives the same counts'); data/looks/*.json; data/examples/canal-lock-place-settings.json.
why: The kit is this lesson turned into code.

lesson: Kit limits found on the courtyard: moss on a roof whose materials hide inside a node setup, run-off streaks on a long garden wall, and different strengths per material for anything but soot could not be set by settings.
source: Textures story log 25; Garden plan 30 builder 3 kit fixes
plugin_evidence: place-kit/README.md line ~78 'Dials and the state are the same for every role ... use look_by_role'; SKILL.md says the same. The garden's three kit fixes (roof materials inside geometry nodes, explicit wall front, per-material dials) are not carried.
why: A stated limit, not a fix.

lesson: At film size shape and designed marks read and shader wear barely does: walls are near black and edge-on so soot and streaks vanish; lean on shape, normal maps, 3D plants; check 100 percent and phone-sized crops.
plugin_evidence: wear-recipes.md 'Honest note: what shows at film size' lines ~97-104; the-required-steps.md 'no two siblings alike'; build-and-paint-a-place 'Traps'.
why: Well carried.

lesson: Weed gates: no plants on wheel tracks, crown, doorsteps or in puddles; lime-bright weeds, pale panels, cold blue doorsteps and over-even cracks were calmed.
plugin_evidence: wear-recipes.md 'Exact-zero gates for plants' and 'Things that already went wrong'; film-settings place_wear.exact_zero_gate_*; audit 'place: keep-out'.
why: Carried and enforced.

lesson: Never put the person's email or name into requests to outside websites: a helper wrote the person's email into the identity line its download scripts sent to Wikipedia and Wikimedia.
plugin_evidence: surface-recipes.md line ~138 'Send a generic client name with the request, never a person's name or address' (Poly Haven only); place-checker.md process mode searches written files for 'email-like strings'; clients use generic User-Agents (render/client.py). No general instruction for any outside website or fetch script.
why: A privacy leak to third parties that no file-scan would catch.

lesson: EEVEE against Cycles on the whole street: the bricks and stone look the same (same scans); Cycles clearly wins on wet ground (mirrored lamps and fronts, warm light reaching the road, clean gutter water); EEVEE keeps joints crisper and shadows with detail; 3.7 s against 14.1 s.
plugin_evidence: rendering-on-rented-cards.md section 1 gives the rule and 'water in view also gives Cycles'; place_card_time estimates. The side-by-side findings and per-picture times are not written.
why: Explains why the rule is Cycles-when-lit rather than always.

lesson: EEVEE streets come out cold blue and Cycles streets warm gold (mostly because EEVEE's light cut-off stops lamp light reaching the road; lowering it makes EEVEE as slow as Cycles), and the painter follows that mood: do not mix renderers within one place or compare across them; Cycles also showed odd Cycles-only effects (a fire drum lit orange, a roof-corner speck, sky dome darkening).
plugin_evidence: No hit for light threshold, cut-off, colour mood by renderer or the Cycles-only oddities in the plugin's docs.
why: Changes the painted mood of a whole film if renderers are mixed.

lesson: When a new version goes into the real film keep the old one beside it so going back is a few renames (the dry paintings were kept beside the wet ones).
plugin_evidence: No hit for keeping the previous version beside the new one or a rollback recipe in the plugin; house-rules.md says only 'never final or v2' for file names.
why: Cheap safety when replacing a person's approved asset.

lesson: A spend record was damaged by writing it through the shell: the '$0' inside 'US$0.048' was read as a command name; write money files with a quoted here-document or from Python.
plugin_evidence: No hit for dollar-sign or shell-quoting problems; plan_budget.py ledger exists but its docs do not warn about writing it through a shell.
why: Corrupted ledgers undermine the money checks.

lesson: Before blaming a change for a faint speckle, run the OLD version twice: one scene came out two ways from run to run even with the old stage code.
plugin_evidence: No hit for run-to-run variation or testing the baseline twice; the plugin tests only that finishing twice gives the same counts.
why: Stops a wrong root cause from being written into the notes.

lesson: Pay-per-second rendering: a worker (card) starts only when a job waits and stops about 5 s after; cold start 20-22 s, warm under a second; RTX 4090 about US$1.10 an hour; Cycles on the card through OptiX (128 samples 5.2 s).
plugin_evidence: rendering-on-rented-cards.md sections 2-3 and 8 (measured numbers); place_render.card_dollars_per_hour 1.1.
why: Carried with measured numbers and dates.

lesson: Rented-machine failure modes: the provider's web address refused Python's default name, 135 single files took 9 minutes (now one bundle), the official Blender site refused so mirror sites with a checksum were used, community cards vanish between asking and starting (three tries), and on one community host Cycles ran on 25 processor cores.
plugin_evidence: rendering-on-rented-cards.md 'A folder goes up as one bundle' (line ~84), section 7 item 2 and blender-5-traps.md item 8 (25 cores, prove the card with a tiny Cycles picture); render/client.py retries with a generic User-Agent. Mirrors with checksum and 'three tries' for community cards are not documented (the person sets the card up).
why: Mostly set-up knowledge for the person.

lesson: When the balance ran down to US$0.13 the cards took no jobs while workers showed idle: check the balance first and stop if jobs wait more than 5 minutes.
plugin_evidence: rendering-on-rented-cards.md section 7 items 1 and 3; place-renderer.md 'The stop rule'; film-settings place_render.jobs_waiting_stop_minutes 5.
why: A real two-hour stall.

lesson: When finished, say what is still running and billing (endpoint set to zero workers at the person's request, stores about US$0.006 an hour, balance), and switch the endpoint back on before the next render.
source: Textures story 'Where things stand' (22 October 15:27) and log 31
plugin_evidence: place-renderer.md 'Never purge the queue and never change the endpoint'; rendering-on-rented-cards.md says workers stop 5 s after the last job. No instruction to report what is left running or to honour a request to switch the endpoint off.
why: Money hygiene at the end of a job.

lesson: The estimate is not a bill: the provider's hourly bill lags and came out above estimates (US$1.13 against about 1.6-1.8 own estimate over time); idle standby workers cost nothing; read charges from the provider's history.
plugin_evidence: rendering-on-rented-cards.md lines ~35-37 'the provider's own bill is the only truth ... never promise a cost from seconds alone'; tips section 16 items 3-4 (read real charges from fal's history).
why: Carried; the idle-standby-is-free detail is not.

lesson: Money limits are set by the person and checked by someone else: stamp test limit US$1.00, repaint under US$0.30, concept images US$15, 'US$20, ask free'; a checker confirmed exactly N calls against fal's history; prices doubled between plan and purchase.
plugin_evidence: LLM tips and tricks.md section 16 (live price before each batch, count every picture sent, running total from the allowance start, 'a vague reply is not a yes'); plan_budget.py ledger refuses a step larger than what is left; place-checker.md process mode.
why: Strongly carried.

lesson: A message sent to a running paid helper woke a second copy of it, which made 8 extra paid calls (about US$0.70 of the total) before it stopped: never message a helper that spends money; check its status first.
plugin_evidence: No hit for waking, second copy or messaging a running helper in the plugin (the workflow build-a-place sends no messages).
why: A direct money leak the ledger does not catch until after the fact.

lesson: Study the existing scene with rays BEFORE rebuilding: a veranda step 23 cm in the air, bridge piers 2-7 cm short, wall caps 6.5 cm up, roof 22 cm off its posts, a lantern glow box buried in stone, 77 deck faces fighting a plinth; none visible at the hero camera.
plugin_evidence: construction-and-scale.md 'The scene study before building' (~103-108) and worked-examples 'What a ray check found'; tips section 8a item 1.
why: Fully carried, with the numbers.

lesson: The audit scripts also check per-object material overrides (object-linked slots after the pigment tool) and unused material slots, and sample ground contact at box corners and edges, not only the lowest points.
plugin_evidence: construction-and-scale.md 'Ground seating' reads the same five points under the box that seat_on_ground uses; no hit for object-linked slots or unused slots.
why: Contact sampling is carried; slot hygiene is not.

lesson: Rank improvements by what a viewer notices: each element's share of the picture (measured on a flat-colour ID map from the same camera) times how wrong it looks, then build in that order.
plugin_evidence: No hit for ranking by share of the picture; style-rule-and-measures.md uses flat-colour region maps only for detail-energy measures.
why: Tells a builder where limited time shows most.

lesson: When the look is a real choice (painted add-on look or realistic like the street) build both as a switch when drawing is cheap, and say which one leads if the person says nothing.
plugin_evidence: No hit; the plugin's looks (kept, lived_in, neglected, derelict) are about wear, not about painted versus realistic.
why: A decision pattern, not a technical rule.

lesson: The person's painted-look rules from the add-on: 'No rounded smooth curves. Just edges and flat surfaces that approximate a curve', broad few unequal colour passages, marks that differ by material, chiselled unequal planes, short mineral marks, depth by colour and selective edge loss; whole-image comparison before details.
source: Garden plan 30 section 4 and Textures log 30
plugin_evidence: kit/place-kit/SOURCES-AND-LICENCES.md lines 31-32 say only the add-on's 'rules they teach' were taken, but searching for chisel, flat planes, rounded smooth, selective edge or mineral finds only 'mineral veins as a few big marks' in surface-recipes.md; the style note template (data/templates/style_note.md) asks for these per place but carries none.
why: These are the person's standing art-direction words for faceted painted looks.

lesson: Build large places as stage files with owners: each builder delivers stage_<name>.py with apply(options) that works on the open start scene, keeps names others rely on, tags objects with owner and role, puts new objects in its own collection, gives new objects a placeholder material, and never renames what it does not own; the final step runs the stages in order and diffs ownership.
plugin_evidence: kit/place-kit/data/templates/stage_template.py; README 'Building in parts'; place-builder.md; `combine`, `fingerprint`, `ownership-diff`; objects carry place_owner and place_role in collections 'Place: <owner>'.
why: The plugin's design is this plan.

lesson: Draw once with each light on its own layer (sun, sky, fill, hall glow, lantern) into a multi-layer EXR so glow can be rebalanced and the picture regraded afterwards for free; light groups are Cycles-only, must add up to the normal picture, caustics off, bloom only above 1.0.
plugin_evidence: style-rule-and-measures.md 'light groups ... add up to the picture, within 2 percent (measured)' and film-settings place_measures.light_group_sum_error_max; no instruction or tool to render light groups or write the EXR.
why: Saves a paid redraw when only the glow balance is wrong.

lesson: Record engine, device, samples, seed, view transform, exposure, size, camera, seconds and a file hash for every picture and keep failed attempts.
source: Garden plan 30 sections 4 and 6 (the add-on's own advice)
plugin_evidence: rendering-on-rented-cards.md line ~107 'Save next to every picture: engine, device, samples, seed, view transform, exposure, size, camera, seconds, Blender version and the SHA-256'; `render` writes the log. 'Keep failed attempts' is not stated.
why: Carried except for the failed-attempts habit.

lesson: Poly Haven scans: pick by drawing a small test plate, not by thumbnail; use 1k maps and pack images; box projection when nothing has UVs; never use a normal map and a bump on the same surface; do not add weathering moss on a scan that already carries moss; world-position mapping for instanced tiles; tiling is the danger on a 16 percent ground area.
source: Garden plan 30 builder 3 part A and section 13
plugin_evidence: surface-recipes.md lines ~138-152 (test plate first, open every picture at full size, generic client name, hide repeats rule 6, UV rule 5) and place_surfaces.bump_leftover_strength_max 0.3. No rule against doubling moss on a mossy scan or against normal plus bump together.
why: Half carried; the moss doubling is easy to repeat.

lesson: Make the weathering shade logic follow the scene's real sun lamp (the kit assumed north is +y and a fixed latitude/azimuth).
source: Garden plan 30 section 5 note and builder 3 part B
plugin_evidence: place_kit/wear/masks.py line 35 SUN_AZIMUTH_DEGREES = 135.0 and light.py TOWARD_SUN_AZIMUTH_DEGREES = 135.0: the shade masks assume a fixed sun and only match when the kit adds its own sun; a scene with its own sun lamp is not read.
why: Moss and soot would sit on the wrong sides of a scene lit from another direction.
